messages:
tess: opened a tiny PR to add an "edge case" section for provisioning where teams combine isolation tags + autoscale surge fallback. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/4788. Goal: one short YAML example, a TS SDK one-liner, and a sentence linking to eviction model and SLA table. can people quick-review?

sam: reading now. i like the idea. make sure we show the fallback order: surge -> burst -> reserved in plain english. that's often what confuses folks.

marta: agree. small copy nit: use `isolation_tags` (list) in the example and show mapping from old `tenant_label`. also use `target_utilization_pct` not `threshold_pct`.

kevin: adding a TS SDK snippet suggestion for the docs (one line):

```ts
await client.capacity.applyPolicy({tenantId: 'team-sparrow', poolType: 'burst', policy: {target_utilization_pct: 70, cooldown_seconds: 300, isolation_tags: ['team-sparrow']}})
```

kevin: kept it compact so readers can paste. will also add a Go example if folks want.

sam: please add the one-sentence SLA caveat: "Reserved pools provide a latency SLA; surge and burst pools are preemptible and have no latency SLA." short and explicit. also add a one-row mapping table for migration: `tenant_label -> isolation_tags[0]`.

marta: tiny YAML example I'm proposing for the edge-case section:

```yaml
pool:
  name: team-sparrow-burst
  type: burst
  target_utilization_pct: 70
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  isolation_tags:
    - team-sparrow
fallback_policy:
  order: [surge, burst, reserved]
```

marta: added an inline link to eviction-model and a one-line pointer to the SLA table. kept everything < 15 lines per docs-bot.

docs-bot: Style check: examples <= 15 lines, use present tense, link internal topics, and prefer `target_utilization_pct` + `cooldown_seconds`. :white_check_mark:

tess: thanks all. i'll incorporate the wording, the TS snippet, the YAML sample, and the migration mapping then merge after CI. ping me if you want the Go snippet included too before merge."
